title: M2 dual literature audit: (A) Danesh 2611.10726 (Weil two-interval criterion, 2026-11-07) VERIFIED VALID - RH <-> Cauchy-Schwarz on subexponentially-shrinking Weil pairs; pole-obstruction lemma sound; no RH claim; M2 wall and terminal face UNCHANGED; formal unit queued. (B) Ismail S(T) finite-height bounds (Zenodo 23301655 v3, 2026-10-11) VERIFIED - row 2 |S(T)| <= 0.134791 log T + 0.159606 log log T + 1.505817 (T >= e), M(3e12) = 5.9143 re-verified; N(T)-form 2.380817; NAMED INPUT [IS] at the frontier scale; NO FACE CONSUMPTION
body:
TWO AUDITS, executed while W81/CE81 closed (the overlap model extends to the M2 lane: lane M5 = certified windows; lane M2 = literature against the pinned wall).

(A) DANEH ARXIV 2611.10726 (Payam Danesh, Polytechnic of Turin; v1 2026-11-07; 'A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis'; 1,330 KB). CLAIM: RH is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality R(f,g) = |B(f,g)|/sqrt(Q(f)Q(g)) <= 1 for every pair of nonzero C_c^infty test functions supported in [0, w(L)] and [L - w(L), L] with w(L) -> 0 and log(1/w(L)) = o(L) (subexponential shrink), at all sufficiently large spans L. A zero rho_0 = beta_0 + i gamma_0 with beta_0 > 1/2 forces R(f,g) > e^{eta L} at arbitrarily large L for every 0 < eta < beta_0 - 1/2 (quantitative violation); reciprocal width w(L) = 1/L included. The cross term is expressed arithmetically (Eq 36): B(g,f) = integral k(u)(e^{u/2} + e^{-u/2} - e^{-u/2}/(1-e^{-2u})) du over u in [L-2w(L), L] MINUS the prime-power sum over the MOVING interval [e^{L-2w(L)}, e^L] - so the criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish RH.
AUDIT (end-to-end, all lemmas re-derived): (1) Theorem 4.1 (RH => R <= 1): under RH, -z_rho_bar = z_rho and B(f,g) is the l2 inner product of the square-summable sequences (H_f(z_rho)) over zeros; convergence from |H_f(sigma+iy)| <= C(1+|y|)^{-r} (all r) and N(T) << (1+T)log(2+T); Cauchy-Schwarz. VERIFIED. (2) Lemma 2 (localization): decompose h into O_A(m) partition pieces of width 2/m, m = ceil(4/w(t+C_A)); each translated pair (u_j, tau_t u_k) after left-end shift is supported in [0, 2/m] and [L_jk - 2/m, L_jk] with L_jk = t + (k-j+2)/m in [t-C_A, t+C_A] and w(L_jk) >= 2/m (w non-increasing) - so each piece pair is admissible at its own span and the hypothesis applies; the diagonal |Q(u_j)| << log(2+m)/m from the (1+|y|/m)^{-4} decay against zero counting; sum over O_A(m^2) pairs gives |B(tau_t h, h)| <= C m log(2+m) e^{eta t}; log(m log m) = o(t) via (12) gives O(e^{(eta+eps) t}) for all h. VERIFIED (the admissibility geometry - left piece [0,2/m], right piece [L_jk-2/m, L_jk] - is the correct one; no overhang). (3) Lemma 3 (pole obstruction): for real even h, F_h(t) = B(tau_t h, h) = sum_rho H_h(z_rho)^2 e^{t z_rho}; the Laplace identity int_0^inf F_h e^{-st} dt = sum_rho H_h(z_rho)^2/(s - z_rho) is termwise justified for Re s > 1/2 UNCONDITIONALLY - the (27) estimate divides by (Re s - 1/2) as a lower bound on (Re s - Re z_rho), which is positive because |Re z_rho| = |beta - 1/2| < 1/2 for all zeros (the critical strip, unconditionally); meromorphic continuation with simple poles, non-zero residue m_0 H_h(z_0)^2 (H_h(z_0) != 0 chosen by shrinking a unit bump); if F_h = O(e^{alpha t}) with alpha < Re z_0, the Laplace integral is holomorphic on Re s > alpha and the identity theorem (applied to M - I on the connected strip Re s > alpha, where M is meromorphic and its poles in the strip include z_0) contradicts the pole. VERIFIED (one precision note for the record: the paper's step 'identity theorem extends from Re s > 1/2' is best read as the meromorphic-difference identity theorem on the connected half-plane Re s > alpha; no conclusion changes). (4) Theorem 4.2 (off-line zero => violations) by contrapositive via Lemma 2 (any eventual R <= e^{eta L} hypothesis forces F_h = O(e^{(eta+eps) t}) for every real h, contradicting Lemma 3 at alpha = eta + eps < beta_0 - 1/2). LOGIC VERIFIED. (5) Arithmetic form (34)-(36): multiplicative Guinand-Weil with phi(x) = x^{-1/2} k(log x) vanishing on (0,1]; phi(1) = 0 and the phi(1/x) term vanish (k supported in [L-2w, L] subset (0, inf)); the pole integral becomes int k(u) e^{-u/2}/(1-e^{-2u}) du under x = e^u; M_phi(rho) = H_g(z_rho) overline{H_f(-z_rho_bar)} so the zero sum IS B(g,f); the prime-power sum runs over e^{L-2w(L)} <= n <= e^L (moving multiplicative interval). VERIFIED. (6) Corollary 5 (violating pair => negative diagonal Q(u - eps v) = 2(1 - R) < 0 for real f,g, B real on real pairs by Z-conjugation symmetry): sound, and the paper honestly flags that comparing to a negative Rayleigh quotient needs an extra norm estimate it does not claim. VERDICT: the criterion is VALID - a genuine new reformulation of RH in Weil-kernel language; it is an IF AND ONLY IF (equivalence), NOT a proof; proving the uniform arithmetic inequality in (36) is exactly as hard as RH itself. EFFECTS: NO RH CLAIM; the pinned M2 wall {theta | 4/7 < theta} is UNAFFECTED (criterion is orthogonal to zero-density exponents); the terminal face is NOT reduced - by 0288-style logic the criterion is another named face-of-RH in the kernel language (like the 0288 split is one in the census+absolute language). FORMAL UNIT QUEUED (D-lane, 'D1C'): formalize (i) the Weil form Q(f), B(f,g) over the abstract zero set with convergence from in-tree zero counting, (ii) the RH => C-S direction (ii) the pole-obstruction lemma as a pure complex-analysis statement (Laplace transform of an O(e^{alpha t}) function + meromorphic continuation + identity theorem + non-trivial pole => not O(e^{alpha t})); the pole-obstruction lemma is self-contained enough for a first standalone unit. Not executed this turn (multi-unit construction; the M5 overlap keeps the machine lane full).

(B) ISMAIL, 'Explicit bounds for S(T) at finite heights' (Zenodo 23301655, v3, published 2026-10-11; Mesut Ismail; Ismail_S_finite_heights.pdf, 9 pp, md5 cb0b2521f6adc30ee98797e03f765d8d). CLAIM (Theorem 1.1): for all T >= e and each of nine rows of Table 1, |S(T)| <= C1 log T + C2 log log T + C3; the row selected at T_opt = 3e12 (row 2) gives |S(T)| <= 0.134791 log T + 0.159606 log log T + 1.505817 for all T >= e. Corollary 1.4 (zero-counting form): N(T) - (T/2pi) log(T/(2pi e)) <= 0.134791 log T + 0.159606 log log T + 2.380817 for T >= e. Corollary 1.3 (gap bound): normalized gap s_n <= 1 + 2 M(gamma_{n+1}) + E(gamma_{n+1}) <= 12.83 at T_RH = 3e12 (vs 13.95 from Bellotti-Wong). Proposition 1.2: M(T) beats EVERY Bellotti-Wong tabulated bound on [30 610 046 000, 1e200] by 0.508% to 8.965% (7.4% at T0, 8.7% at 3e12, 8.9% at 1e13). AUDIT: (1) FINAL QUANTITATIVE INEQUALITY VERIFIED: row 2 rigorous values C1 = 0.13479015, C2 = 0.15960505, C3 = 1.50581607, rounded UP in the sixth decimal -> 0.134791, 0.159606, 1.505817 (each rounding direction checked: raw <= printed); M(3e12) re-computed from the printed constants: 0.134791*ln(3e12) + 0.159606*ln ln(3e12) + 1.505817 = 3.872496 + 0.535980 + 1.505817 = 5.914293, matching the paper's M(T_RH) = 5.9143 (row 2) to 4 decimals; C3 + 7/8 = 1.505817 + 0.875 = 2.380817 exactly as printed. (2) INPUTS all published/refereed: Hiary-Patel-Yang |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.618 t^{1/6} log t [10] (rows 1-6), Patel-Yang sub-Weyl 66.7 t^{27/164} [15] (rows 7-9), Hoo-Teo |zeta(1+it)| <= 1/2 log t + 0.6633 [11] absorbed as the 1-line input c1(Q0) = 1/2 + 0.6633/log Q0 with Q0 = 1e9 giving c1 = 0.5320075... <= 0.532008 (arithmetic re-verified: 0.6633/20.723265... = 0.0320075), Yang 1.546 t^{1/(2k-2)} log t [24], the Bellotti-Wong framework [3] (their Table 2 reproduced by the author's code to published precision), low-T extension |S| <= 1 (T<=280), 2 (<=6.8e6), 2.5167 (<= T0 = 3.06e10) standard. (3) CERTIFICATION: every constant a rigorous Arb ball enclosure (200 bits, python-flint, acb_calc_integrate) with radii below 1e-56, rounding up per integer arithmetic (no float step); 69 checks in the public script verify_S_bound.py (repository given); the shifted-form inequalities (3.1)-(3.3) verified for all real t including the |t|<=3 ball-arithmetic check (minimal positive margin 0.147 over 600 subintervals) and the t=0 limit it*zeta(1+it) -> 1. (4) HONESTY: Remark 1.5 ('modest by design'; method is Bellotti-Wong's; contribution is inputs/parameters); the paper flags a MISPRINT in [3] (a stray log log T0 in kappa_3, effect 1.5e-5 on row 2) and a code discrepancy in [3] (denominator, effect 1.9e-6) - audit-grade treatment of the base paper. VERDICT: VALID and rigorously certified; the best explicit |S(T)| bound at finite heights for T0 <= T <= 1e200; the leading coefficient 0.10076 of [3] remains best (Ismail's rows trade leading coefficient for finite-height constants). RELATION TO THE PROGRAM: (i) the row-2 bound is valid for ALL T >= e, hence for EVERY T above the current certified frontier tCE81 = 3 000 175 715 975 (= 3.0001757e12) - it is a uniform, data-free, published upper bound on S on the terminal-face regime: |S(T)| <= 5.9143 at the frontier height and growing only like 0.134791 log T; (ii) it is the strongest such bound exactly at our scale (T_opt = 3e12; M(3e12) = 5.9143 vs 6.475 Bellotti-Wong, 8.7% gain); (iii) the N(T)-form (2.380817) gives |N(T) - (T/2pi)log(T/(2pi e))| <= 6.7893 at T = 3e12 - an independent published consistency input on the global zero count at frontier height (12.36e12 +/- 6.79 zeros below 3e12 vs the pipeline's local chain counts); (iv) NO FACE CONSUMPTION: the terminal face (hs1/E1: the data-free zero-side-scale lower bound / bounded missing-tail quantity above the frontier) is NOT killed by an S bound - the E1 data face shows M_wp growing like -5.815e7 ln t (B = 2 refuted above G), and per 0350 no published theorem supplies the finite ABSOLUTE bound at the zeros; recorded as NAMED INPUT [IS] in S1-A1 with full provenance (Zenodo v3, md5, row constants, certification facts), exactly as the Z78 precedent (0386) treated a strengthened strip: named-input record only, terminal face unchanged. FORMAL UNIT QUEUED (S1A1-lane, 'SIs'): formalize [IS] row 2 as a named input theorem in S4Strip/SWall-adjacent territory and state precisely what the hs1 face would (not) gain from consuming it - a negative result formalized is a win (it pins the wall's boundary).
rh_claim: NO RH CLAIM - (A) Danesh 2611.10726 is a valid EQUIVALENCE (RH <-> uniform Weil two-interval inequality), not a proof; the pinned M2 wall and the terminal face are unchanged; formalization queued (D1C). (B) Ismail Zenodo 23301655 v3 is a valid, Arb-certified explicit S(T)/N(T) bound at the frontier scale, recorded as named input [IS]; it does not consume the terminal face (no published theorem supplies the absolute data-free bound at the zeros - 0350 stands); formalization queued (SIs)
